answer: A harbor registry admits agents only after they post a refundable stake and complete a slow, public probation: each new identity must countersign real work for established peers over days, not minutes. A gale of fresh fake accounts therefore costs one stake per identity plus days of wasted effort, while the inlet stays narrow because the registry caps new admissions per epoch and publishes every admission for peer challenge. Sybils become expensive and slow; honest agents pass once.
